questions.question: What is the main focus of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) scheme launched in 2015?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Girl child survival & education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** scheme was launched on **22 January 2015** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Panipat, Haryana.
 
• The main objective of the scheme is to address the declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)** and promote the survival, protection, and education of the girl child.
 
• The initiative is a tri-ministerial effort involving the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**, the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**, and the **Ministry of Education** (formerly MHRD).
 
• The scheme focuses on generating awareness and improving the efficiency of welfare services intended for girls across India.
 
• **District-level implementation:** The scheme was initially implemented in 100 districts with a low Child Sex Ratio and later expanded to cover all districts in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):** CSR refers to the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the 0-6 age group. A decline in CSR reflects social issues such as gender-based discrimination and female foeticide.
 
• **Key Components of BBBP:**
 
 
• **Advocacy and media campaigns:** To create awareness and change societal attitudes towards the girl child.
 
• **Multi-sectoral interventions:** In targeted districts to ensure access to education and health services for girls.
 
• **Monitoring:** Regular monitoring of CSR and other indicators to evaluate the scheme's impact.
 
 
 
• **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY):** A savings scheme under BBBP that promotes financial security for the girl child by offering attractive interest rates and tax benefits.
 
• **Impact of BBBP:** The scheme has led to significant improvements in CSR in several districts, increased enrollment of girls in schools, and enhanced awareness about gender equality.
 
• **Global Perspective:** BBBP aligns with the United Nations' **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly Goal 5 (Gender Equality) and Goal 4 (Quality Education).

questions.question: Which of the following simple household methods can detect the presence of chalk powder in adulterated wheat flour?

options.text: Mixing with vinegar to observe fizzing reaction
Adding iodine solution to observe color change
Heating over flame to detect odor
Soaking in alcohol to dissolve the chalk

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixing with vinegar to observe fizzing reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chalk powder, primarily composed of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), reacts with acids like vinegar (acetic acid) to produce carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas.
 
• When vinegar is added to adulterated wheat flour containing chalk powder, fizzing or effervescence is observed due to the release of CO₂ gas.
 
• This simple household method is an effective and quick way to detect the presence of chalk powder in wheat flour.
 
• The reaction involved is: CaCO₃ + 2CH₃COOH → Ca(CH₃COO)₂ + H₂O + CO₂↑.
 
• Effervescence or bubbling confirms the presence of calcium carbonate in the adulterated wheat flour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adulteration:** It refers to the practice of adding unwanted substances to food items to increase quantity or reduce production costs, often compromising quality and safety.
 
• **Calcium Carbonate:** A common compound found in chalk, marble, and limestone. It is harmless in small amounts but is considered an adulterant when added to food products like flour.
 
• **Vinegar:** A household acid (acetic acid, CH₃COOH) commonly used in cooking and cleaning, making it a practical tool for such tests.
 
• **Effervescence:** The bubbling or fizzing that occurs due to the release of gas during a chemical reaction, such as the reaction of acids with carbonates.
 
• **Food Safety:** Regular checks for adulterants in food products are crucial to ensuring health and preventing long-term health risks associated with contaminated food.

Consider the following characteristics:

1. High moisture-retaining capacity, often developing deep cracks during dry hot weather.

2.Ideal for tea and apple cultivation due to high fertility and cold climate preference.

3. Rich in lime, iron, magnesia, and alumina, but poor in phosphoric contents.

Which of the above characteristics are primarily associated with Black Soils?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Black soils** exhibit high moisture-retaining capacity, which is why they often develop deep cracks during dry hot weather.
 
• They are rich in lime, iron, magnesia, and alumina, but lack sufficient phosphoric content, making them unique in composition.
 
• These soils are also known as **Regur soils** and are highly suitable for crops such as cotton.
 
• The characteristics listed under points 1 and 3 align strongly with the properties of Black soils.
 
• Point 2 about tea and apple cultivation is more characteristic of soils in cold climates, such as mountain soils, and does not pertain to Black soils.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black Soils:** They are formed from volcanic rocks and are predominantly found in the Deccan plateau regions of India, including Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Moisture Retention:** Black soils are known for their ability to retain moisture, making them ideal for crops like cotton, which require consistent water availability.
 
• **Cracking Phenomenon:** During dry seasons, the soil develops cracks, which helps in aeration and natural tilling of the land.
 
• **Regional Suitability:** Black soils are highly suitable for crops like cotton, sugarcane, pulses, and cereals due to their nutrient profile.
 
• **Other Soil Types:** Mountain soils, unlike Black soils, are suitable for tea and apple cultivation due to their high organic content and cold climate compatibility.

Consider the following statements:

Statement I: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 aimed to promote private sector dominance in all key industries.

Statement II: The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 classified industries into three categories: fully government-owned, mixed sector

with government lead, and private sector.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

options.text: Both statements I and II are incorrect
statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Both statements I and II are correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement I is incorrect:** The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 aimed at strengthening the public sector, not promoting private sector dominance.
 
• **Statement II is correct:** The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 categorized industries into three schedules: exclusively government-owned, mixed public-private sector, and private sector.
 
• The 1956 policy was strongly influenced by the socialist framework, emphasizing the role of the state in industrial development.
 
• The resolution aimed to reduce income inequalities, promote regional balance, and achieve self-reliance in industrial production.
 
• It laid the foundation for India's industrial growth by prioritizing heavy industries and infrastructure development under public ownership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:** This policy was a major shift from the 1948 Industrial Policy, placing significant emphasis on public sector enterprises.
 
• **Three-category classification:**
 
 
• Category A: Industries exclusively reserved for state ownership and operation (e.g., defense, atomic energy).
 
• Category B: Industries where both public and private sectors could operate, but with the public sector taking the lead (e.g., machine tools, fertilizers).
 
• Category C: All other industries left to the private sector but regulated by the state.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 1956 Policy:** It was based on the Nehruvian vision of development and aligned with the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Public Sector Expansion:** The policy led to the establishment of major public sector enterprises like BHEL, SAIL, and NTPC.
 
• **Criticism:** The policy was criticized for excessive bureaucracy, inefficiency in public sector enterprises, and limited scope for private sector growth.

questions.question: Under Chapter V of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, which of the following qualifies as primary evidence?

options.text: A counterpart document executed by one of the parties
A photocopy of the document signed by a clerk
A typed copy of the original document

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A counterpart document executed by one of the parties**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Chapter V of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, primary evidence refers to the **original document itself**, or a counterpart document executed by one of the parties involved in a transaction.
 
• Primary evidence is defined in Section 62 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, and has been adopted in the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, as the most reliable form of evidence.
 
• It is considered **direct evidence** that does not require further corroboration or secondary evidence to prove its authenticity.
 
• The counterpart document executed by one of the parties is treated as primary evidence when it is **authenticated and executed** by the parties involved.
 
• Photocopies, summaries, or typed versions are generally classified as **secondary evidence** unless authenticated under specific provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Evidence:** Original documents or counterparts executed by the parties involved in a transaction.
 
• **Secondary Evidence:** Includes copies, summaries, or reproductions of the original document, which require further authentication.
 
• **Indian Evidence Act, 1872:** The foundational legal framework for evidence in India, defining primary and secondary evidence under Sections 62 and 63.
 
• **Authentication:** The process of verifying the genuineness of a document by confirming its execution by the parties involved.
 
• **Relevance in Legal Proceedings:** Primary evidence is considered more reliable and carries greater probative value in courts compared to secondary evidence.
 
• **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023:** The updated legislation for evidence in India, incorporating modern principles and interpretations of evidence law.

questions.question: Which Chola ruler is credited with the construction of irrigation systems to support agriculture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra Chola I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rajendra Chola I, the son of Raja Raja Chola I, ruled the Chola dynasty from 1014 to 1044 CE and expanded its territory significantly.
 
• He is credited with constructing advanced irrigation systems, including tanks, reservoirs, and canals, to boost agricultural productivity in the Chola Empire.
 
• The Chola rulers, under Rajendra Chola I, focused on water management and utilized river systems like the Kaveri to create sustainable agricultural practices.
 
• Rajendra Chola I established the city of Gangaikonda Cholapuram and built extensive infrastructure to support his empire’s agrarian economy.
 
• His irrigation initiatives were pivotal in transforming the fertile lands of the Tamil region into one of the most prosperous agricultural zones during his reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chola Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chola dynasty was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in Indian history, with its origins tracing back to the 9th century CE.
 
• They were renowned for their contributions to art, architecture, administration, and infrastructure development.
 
• The Cholas built iconic temples such as the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Systems:**
 
 
• Ancient Indian rulers prioritized irrigation systems to ensure sustainable agricultural practices and food security.
 
• Techniques included the use of canals, tanks, and reservoirs for water storage and distribution.
 
• The Kaveri delta region was a crucial area for irrigation development during the Chola period.
 
 
 
• **Gangaikonda Cholapuram:**
 
 
• Rajendra Chola I established Gangaikonda Cholapuram as the capital of the Chola Empire.
 
• The city featured advanced urban planning and infrastructure, including temples and irrigation systems.
 
• It served as a symbol of Chola power and prosperity during his reign.
 
 
 
• **Agrarian Economy:**
 
 
• The Chola dynasty depended heavily on agriculture for economic stability and expansion.
 
• Efficient irrigation systems allowed the cultivation of crops like rice, which was a staple food for the population.
 
• The agrarian economy fueled trade and commerce, making the Chola Empire a prominent player in regional and international trade.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature for Geetanjali?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature for his collection of poems, **Geetanjali**, in 1913.
 
• The Nobel Prize was awarded to Tagore for his "profoundly sensitive, fresh, and beautiful verse," making him the first non-European to receive this honor.
 
• **Geetanjali**, also known as "Song Offerings," is a collection of 103 poems originally written in Bengali and later translated into English by Tagore himself.
 
• Tagore was not only a poet but also a novelist, painter, philosopher, and composer who made significant contributions to Indian and global literature.
 
• His Nobel Prize brought Indian literature into the global spotlight, establishing Tagore as an international literary figure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath Tagore:**

 
 
• Born on 7 May 1861 in Kolkata, Tagore was a polymath who reshaped Bengali literature, music, and art.
 
• He founded **Visva-Bharati University** at Santiniketan, which became a center for cultural and educational exchange.
 
 
 
• **Geetanjali:**
 
 
• Originally written in Bengali, Tagore translated it into English, which led to his Nobel Prize recognition.
 
• The work reflects themes of spirituality, divine love, and human connection.
 
 
 
• **The Nobel Prize:**
 
 
• Established by Alfred Nobel in 1895, it is awarded annually in categories like Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore’s Nobel Prize in 1913 was the first for an Asian in the Literature category.
 
 
 
• **Tagore's Legacy:**
 
 
• Tagore composed the national anthems of both India ("Jana Gana Mana") and Bangladesh ("Amar Shonar Bangla").
 
• He remains a revered figure in Indian and world literature, continuing to inspire generations with his works.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Ramjets operate efficiently at hypersonic speeds.

2. Dual Mode Ramjets can work in both subsonic and supersonic modes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4) 1 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ramjets operate efficiently at hypersonic speeds** (above Mach 5) due to their ability to compress incoming air without moving parts like compressors.
 
• Ramjets are typically used in applications such as missiles or high-speed aircraft, where sustained high-speed operation is required.
 
• The operational efficiency of ramjets decreases at lower speeds because they rely on the forward motion of the vehicle to compress air.
 
• **Statement 1 is correct:** Ramjets are best suited for speeds ranging from Mach 3 to Mach 6.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramjet:** A type of air-breathing jet engine that uses the engine's forward motion to compress incoming air, eliminating the need for a rotary compressor.
 
• **Dual Mode Ramjet (DMRJ):** A propulsion system capable of operating in both ramjet and scramjet modes. It works efficiently at supersonic and hypersonic speeds but not at subsonic speeds, making Statement 2 incorrect.
 
• **Hypersonic Speed:** Refers to speeds greater than Mach 5 (five times the speed of sound). Hypersonic systems include advanced technologies like scramjets and ramjets.
 
• **Scramjet:** A variation of the ramjet engine that operates at hypersonic speeds by allowing supersonic airflow throughout the engine.
 
• **Applications:** Ramjets and scramjets are used in advanced military applications, space exploration, and next-generation high-speed travel.

questions.question: In collaboration with which country is ISRO developing the Trishna satellite for high-resolution thermal infrared imaging of Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**France**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The TRISHNA satellite (Thermal Infrared Imaging Satellite for High-resolution Natural resource Assessment) is being developed jointly by **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation)** and **CNES (National Centre for Space Studies), France**.
 
• It aims to provide **high-resolution thermal infrared imaging** for applications such as water resource management, urban planning, and climate monitoring.
 
• TRISHNA will operate in the **thermal infrared spectrum** and is expected to deliver data with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution.
 
• The satellite builds upon the collaborative legacy of previous ISRO-CNES partnerships, such as the **Megha-Tropiques** and **SARAL** missions.
 
• This mission highlights the growing **India-France space cooperation**, which has spanned over five decades, fostering advancements in Earth observation and space technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermal Infrared Imaging:**

 
 
• Thermal imaging detects heat emitted by objects and is widely used for Earth observation, agriculture, and disaster management.
 
• It helps in understanding land surface temperatures, water body temperatures, and vegetation health.
 
 
 
• **ISRO-CNES Collaboration:**
 
 
• India and France have a long-standing partnership in space programs, beginning with the launch of India’s first satellite, **Aryabhata**, in 1975.
 
• Notable joint missions include Megha-Tropiques (climate monitoring) and SARAL (oceanography).
 
 
 
• **Importance of TRISHNA:**
 
 
• The satellite will assist in climate change studies by providing accurate data on Earth’s heat budget and water cycles.
 
• It will also support sustainable development goals, particularly in agriculture and water management.
 
 
 
• **Earth Observation Satellites:**
 
 
• Earth observation satellites are used to monitor and assess changes in the planet's surface and atmosphere.
 
• Examples include ISRO’s **CARTOSAT** and **RISAT** series, which cater to mapping, disaster management, and defense needs.

questions.question: What is the radius of the striking or shooting circle in hockey?.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14.63 meters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The radius of the striking or shooting circle in hockey is **14.63 meters**, as per the official rules of the International Hockey Federation (FIH).
 
• This circle is often referred to as the "D" or the "shooting circle" due to its semicircular shape.
 
• The striking circle is the area from where players can legally score a goal if the ball is hit within its boundary.
 
• The measurement is taken from the center of the goal line to the outer edge of the circle.
 
• This dimension is standardized for all international hockey games to maintain uniformity in play.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shooting Circle:** The area where players can shoot the ball to score a goal, provided the ball is touched by an attacker inside this zone.
 
• **Penalty Corner:** Awarded to the attacking team for a foul committed by the defending team inside the shooting circle.
 
• **Goal Dimensions:** The width of the goal in field hockey is 3.66 meters, and its height is 2.14 meters.
 
• **Field Dimensions:** A standard field hockey pitch measures 91.4 meters in length and 55 meters in width.
 
• **Field Markings:** In addition to the striking circle, the pitch includes 23-meter lines, a centerline, and sidelines for game organization and rule enforcement.

questions.question: Why does a skilled cricketer move his hands backwards while catching a fast-moving ball?

options.text: To apply a greater opposing force on the ball for a quick stop.
To reduce the force by increasing the time over which momentum changes.
To increase the speed of the ball during impact.
To decrease the weight of the ball using gravity.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To reduce the force by increasing the time over which momentum changes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a cricketer moves his hands backward while catching a fast-moving ball, the time duration of the impact increases. This results in the momentum of the ball changing more gradually.
 
• According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, force is inversely proportional to the time over which the change in momentum occurs. Increasing the time reduces the force applied on the hands.
 
• Reducing the force during impact helps in minimizing the risk of injury to the cricketer's hands.
 
• This technique utilizes the concept of "Impulse," which is the product of force and the time duration of its application.
 
• The backward movement of hands ensures that the ball's momentum is brought to zero in a controlled manner, enhancing the efficiency and safety of the catch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**

 
 
• Newton's Second Law states that Force (F) = Mass (m) × Acceleration (a). It also relates to momentum as F = Δp/Δt, where Δp is the change in momentum and Δt is the time interval.
 
• The concept of impulse is derived from this law, where Impulse = Force × Time = Change in Momentum.
 
 
 
• **Momentum:** Momentum (p) is the product of an object's mass and velocity (p = mv). It is a vector quantity and is conserved in the absence of external forces.
 
• **Impulse:** Impulse is the measure of the change in momentum of an object when a force acts over a time interval. It explains the importance of increasing the time of impact to reduce the applied force.
 
• **Safety in Sports:** Techniques like moving hands backward while catching are designed to minimize injuries by distributing the force over a longer time, aligning with the principles of physics.
 
• **Real-World Applications:** The same principle is applied in car crash safety mechanisms like airbags and crumple zones, which increase the time of impact to reduce force and prevent severe injuries.

• **Treaty of Paris (1763):**

• **French Settlements in India:** The major French trading posts included Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Chandernagore, and Yanam.
 
• **Impact on British-French Rivalry:** The treaty marked a significant step towards British domination in India, minimizing French interference in Indian affairs.
 
• **Colonial Conflicts in India:** The Anglo-French rivalry in India, also known as the Carnatic Wars (1746–1763), was a key factor leading to the treaty's terms.

questions.question: Which body has the power to amend the Union and State power distribution under the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the Indian Constitution, the power to amend the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and State governments lies with the **Parliament**.
 
• Such amendments are carried out under Article 368, which provides the procedure for amending the Constitution.
 
• Any amendment related to the Union-State power distribution requires the approval of both houses of Parliament, followed by ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.
 
• These amendments are considered "Constitutional Amendments" and typically require a two-thirds majority in both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
 
• The process ensures that any change in the power distribution is conducted democratically and with extensive deliberation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 368:** It provides the detailed procedure for amending the Constitution, including changes to Union-State power distribution.
 
• **Federal Structure:** India follows a quasi-federal system where legislative, executive, and financial powers are divided between the Union and State governments under the Seventh Schedule.
 
• **Seventh Schedule:** It categorizes subjects into three lists—Union List, State List, and Concurrent List—to delineate the powers of the Union and State governments.
 
• **Concurrent Amendments:** Changes affecting both Union and State powers require ratification by at least 50% of state legislatures to ensure cooperation and consensus.
 
• **Judicial Review:** The Supreme Court has the power to review Constitutional Amendments to ensure they do not violate the "Basic Structure Doctrine" of the Constitution.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. All-India Services common to Union & states.

2. Controlled by state governments only.

Which of the above statements is/are true?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **All-India Services**, such as the IAS (Indian Administrative Service), IPS (Indian Police Service), and IFoS (Indian Forest Service), are common to both the Union and State governments.
 
• These services are governed by the **All-India Services Act, 1951**, ensuring uniformity in administration.
 
• Officers of All-India Services are recruited centrally by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), but their services are allocated to various states.
 
• While they serve in states, their administrative control and career progression are jointly managed by the **Union Government and the respective State Governments**.
 
• The second statement is incorrect because All-India Services are not controlled solely by state governments; they are under dual control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **All-India Services Act, 1951:** This act provides the legal framework for managing All-India Services. It establishes the joint control of Union and States over these services.
 
• **Recruitment Process:** The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts competitive examinations to recruit candidates for All-India Services.
 
• **Dual Control:** Officers of All-India Services work in states but are also subject to central government rules regarding promotions, transfers, and disciplinary actions.

__

• The objective of these statements is to provide a roadmap for fiscal consolidation, ensuring fiscal discipline and long-term economic stability.
 
• The Finance Minister also reviews compliance with the targets set under the FRBM Act, such as fiscal deficit and revenue deficit, and reports deviations, if any, to Parliament.
 
• These statements aim to keep fiscal management aligned with the principles of prudence, sustainability, and intergenerational equity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act:**

 
 
• It was enacted in 2003 to institutionalize financial discipline and reduce fiscal deficits in India.
 
• The Act sets limits on the fiscal deficit and public debt of the government, aiming to achieve a balanced budget over time.
 
• It was amended in 2018 to include a fiscal deficit target of 3% of GDP by March 2021.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit:**
 
 
• It is the difference between total government expenditure and its total revenue (excluding borrowings).
 
• High fiscal deficits can lead to inflationary pressures, whereas low deficits ensure fiscal sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Deficit:**
 
 
• The revenue deficit refers to the excess of the government's revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
 
• A high revenue deficit indicates that the government is borrowing to meet its operational expenses.
 
 
 
• **Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement:**
 
 
• It projects three-year rolling targets for key fiscal indicators like revenue deficit, fiscal deficit, and debt levels.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement:**
 
 
• It outlines the government's strategy to achieve fiscal objectives and manage public finances.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best captures the essence of Malthus' theory as outlined in the passage?

options.text: the natural imbalance between food supply and population growth leads to unavoidable hardships unless population is controlled
Voluntary checks on population are more effective than natural calamities in curbing overpopulation.
Population grows in arithmetic progression, while food production grows geometrically
Agricultural production can grow faster than population with technological advancement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the natural imbalance between food supply and population growth leads to unavoidable hardships unless population is controlled**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thomas Malthus proposed that population growth tends to outstrip food supply, leading to resource scarcity and societal hardships.
 
• He argued that population grows exponentially while food production grows only arithmetically, creating a natural imbalance.
 
• Malthus emphasized the importance of controlling population growth through preventive measures like moral restraint.
 
• Without such checks, he believed that natural calamities like famine, disease, and war would serve as corrective forces to reduce population size.
 
• Malthus' theory underscores the critical need for sustainable population management to avoid societal collapse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Malthusian Theory:** Proposed in 1798 in his book "An Essay on the Principle of Population," Malthus suggested that unchecked population growth leads to poverty and social unrest.
 
• **Exponential vs Arithmetic Growth:** Population grows exponentially (doubling over time), while food supply grows arithmetically (linear increase), creating an imbalance.
 
• **Preventive Checks:** Measures like delayed marriage, celibacy, and family planning to control population growth.
 
• **Positive Checks:** Natural disasters, famine, disease, and conflict that reduce population when preventive measures are ineffective.
 
• **Criticism:** Advances in agricultural technology and economic development have challenged Malthus' predictions, making them less applicable in modern contexts.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:

Statement 1: The temperature in Troposphere decreases at the rate of 1°C for every 165 meters of height.

Statement 2: The temperature in mesosphere starts to decrease with the increase in altitude and reaches up to -100°C at around 80 km.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1** is correct: The temperature in the troposphere decreases at an approximate rate of **6.5ºC per kilometer**, which is equivalent to 1ºC for every 165 meters of altitude. This phenomenon is called the **environmental lapse rate.**
 
• **Statement 2** is correct: In the **mesosphere**, the temperature decreases with altitude, reaching around **-100ºC** near its upper boundary at approximately 80 kilometers above the Earth's surface.
 
• The troposphere is the lowest layer of Earth's atmosphere, where **weather phenomena occur** and temperature decreases due to reduced air density and pressure.
 
• The mesosphere is the middle layer of the atmosphere, characterized by decreasing temperatures and is considered the **coldest layer** of Earth's atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Troposphere:**

 
 
• The troposphere extends up to about **8-15 kilometers** above the Earth's surface, depending on the geographical location (higher at the equator).
 
• It contains approximately **75% of the atmosphere's mass** and nearly all the water vapor.
 
• Temperature decreases as altitude increases due to the **adiabatic cooling** of rising air.
 
 
 
• **Mesosphere:**
 
 
• The mesosphere lies above the stratosphere and extends from approximately **50 to 80 kilometers** above the Earth's surface.
 
• It is known for the presence of **noctilucent clouds** and meteors that burn up due to atmospheric friction.
 
• Temperatures in the mesosphere drop significantly, reaching as low as **-100ºC** due to low air density.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Lapse Rate:**
 
 
• This refers to the rate at which air temperature decreases with altitude in the troposphere, averaging **6.5ºC per kilometer.**
 
• It varies based on local weather conditions, humidity, and geographical factors.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Layers:**
 
 
• Earth's atmosphere is divided into five layers: **Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere, and Exosphere.**
 
• Each layer has distinct temperature and pressure profiles.

__
 
• During the 18th century, the British economy experienced rapid capital accumulation, leading to the Industrial Revolution.
 
• This capital was reinvested primarily in industrial development, paving the way for advancements in machinery, production techniques, and infrastructure.

questions.question: Who among the following is the final interpreter of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Supreme Court of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial authority in the country and serves as the final interpreter of the Constitution.
 
• It has the authority to review the constitutionality of laws passed by the legislature and actions taken by the executive.
 
• The Supreme Court's role as the guardian of the Constitution ensures that fundamental rights are protected and upheld.
 
• Article 141 of the Indian Constitution states that the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India.
 
• Through its power of judicial review, the Supreme Court can strike down any law or executive action that violates the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review:** The power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts and executive orders. It is a crucial mechanism to maintain the supremacy of the Constitution.
 
• **Fundamental Rights:** Rights guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution, including the right to equality, freedom, and protection against discrimination.
 
• **Article 32:** Allows individuals to approach the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of fundamental rights, making it a defender of constitutional rights.
 
• **Writ Jurisdiction:** The Supreme Court can issue writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari to ensure justice and uphold fundamental rights.
 
• **Constitution Bench:** A bench of at least five judges of the Supreme Court is constituted to decide significant constitutional matters, ensuring authoritative interpretation of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following accurately describes the statutory responsibilities of the Lokpal under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013?

options.text: The Lokpal is mandated to provide the President with an annual report, which will be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
The Lokpal operates under the direct administrative control of the Prime Minister's Office.
The Lokpal must submit regular reports to the Election Commission for public disclosure.

The Lokpal is a constitutional body tasked with making final judgments in corruption cases 

Not Answered

• The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, mandates the Lokpal to submit an annual report to the President of India.
 
• This report includes details of its activities, inquiries, and investigations conducted during the year.
 
• The President is required to lay this annual report before both Houses of Parliament for transparency and accountability.
 
• The Lokpal is a statutory body, not a constitutional body, established to investigate allegations of corruption against public servants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Composition of Lokpal:** The Lokpal consists of a chairperson and up to eight members, of whom at least 50% must be judicial members and 50% must be from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, minorities, or women.
 
• **Jurisdiction:** The Lokpal has jurisdiction over public servants, including the Prime Minister (with certain safeguards), Ministers, Members of Parliament, and Group A, B, C, and D officials.
 
• **Independence:** The Lokpal is an independent body and is not under the administrative control of any government office, including the Prime Minister's Office.
 
• **Reporting Mechanism:** By submitting its annual report to the President, the Lokpal ensures transparency and public accountability in its functioning.

questions.question: Which of the following methods was used by the villagers during the Chipko Movement?

• Villagers, primarily women, used the method of hugging trees (literally embracing them) to prevent contractors from cutting them down.
 
• The movement gained momentum in 1973 in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand (then part of Uttar Pradesh).
 
• It was inspired by Gandhian principles of non-violent resistance and sought to protect forests, which were critical for the livelihood and ecological stability of the local communities.
 
• This grassroots effort played a significant role in influencing environmental policies in India, including the Forest Conservation Act of 1980.

• **Role of Women:** Women played a central role in the movement, as they were the primary stakeholders dependent on forests for fuel, fodder, and water.
 
• **Key Leaders:** Prominent leaders of the movement included environmentalist Sunderlal Bahuguna, Chandi Prasad Bhatt, and Gaura Devi, who mobilized local communities for the cause.
 
• **Impact on Policy:** The Chipko Movement led to a 15-year ban on cutting trees in the Himalayan forests by the government and influenced India's environmental conservation policies.
 
• **Global Influence:** The movement became a symbol of environmental activism worldwide, inspiring similar movements in other countries to protect natural resources.

questions.question: An electric kettle is rated 2.2kW 220V. It the cost of electricity is ₹4 per unit (kwh), what is the cost of boiling water for 30 minutes?

• **Cost Calculation:** The cost of electricity is determined by multiplying the energy consumed (kWh) by the rate per unit.
 
• **Efficiency Considerations:** Electric kettles are designed to convert electrical energy into heat with high efficiency, minimizing energy losses.
 
• **Daily Usage:** Understanding energy consumption helps households manage electricity bills effectively and promotes energy-saving practices.

questions.question: The highest rainfall in India gets recorded in the Khasi and Jaintia Hills. In which state will you find these hills?

__
 
• The Khasi and Jaintia Hills are located in the state of **Meghalaya**, India.
 
• These hills experience extremely high rainfall due to their proximity to the **Bay of Bengal** and the orographic effect caused by the monsoon winds hitting the hills.
 
• **Mawsynram** in the Khasi Hills is known as the wettest place on Earth, with an annual rainfall exceeding 11,000 mm.

• **Orographic Rainfall:** This type of rainfall occurs when moist air is lifted as it moves over a mountain range, leading to condensation and heavy precipitation on the windward side.
 
• **Cherrapunji:** Located in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, it was previously known as the wettest place on Earth before Mawsynram took the title.
 
• **Monsoon Winds:** The Southwest Monsoon is the primary reason for heavy rainfall in Meghalaya, as it carries moisture-laden winds from the Indian Ocean.
 
• **Biodiversity:** Meghalaya's forests are rich in plant and animal species, including rare orchids and endemic wildlife, due to the high rainfall and unique topography.
 
• **Tourism:** The heavy rainfall and scenic beauty of the Khasi and Jaintia Hills attract tourists to popular locations such as living root bridges, caves, and waterfalls.

questions.question: In a two-sector economy, households provide factors of production to firms and receive income. If households save part of this income, what is affected ?

options.text: The circular flow becomes a leakage

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The circular flow becomes a leakage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a two-sector economy, households earn income by providing factors of production (labor, capital, land, etc.) to firms, creating a circular flow of income.
 
• When households save a portion of their income instead of spending it, the money is withdrawn from the economic cycle, which is termed as a "leakage."
 
• Leakages reduce the flow of money within the economy, potentially leading to lower demand for goods and services.
 
• This phenomenon can impact overall economic activity by decreasing firm revenues and production levels in the absence of compensatory investments or government interventions.
 
• In a two-sector model, savings must equal investments to maintain equilibrium, highlighting the importance of reinjecting savings into the economy through productive investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Circular Flow of Income:** This refers to the continuous movement of money, resources, and goods between households and firms in an economy.
 
• **Leakages:** Any withdrawal of spending from the circular flow, such as savings, taxes, or imports, that reduces the overall economic activity.
 
• **Injections:** Additions to the circular flow, such as investments, government spending, or exports, which stimulate economic activity.
 
• **Two-Sector Model:** A simplified economic model that includes only households and firms, excluding government and foreign trade, to analyze basic economic interactions.
 
• **Equilibrium in Two-Sector Economy:** Equilibrium is achieved when total leakages (savings) are equal to total injections (investments), ensuring a stable flow of income and output.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Square Kilometer Array (SKA) is correct?

options.text: It is managed entirely by the European Space Agency.
It aims to explore cosmic magnetism and dark matter.
It focuses solely on detecting visible light.
It will consist of a single telescope in India.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Square Kilometer Array (SKA) is an international project aimed at building the world’s largest radio telescope.
 
• One of its primary objectives is to explore cosmic mysteries such as **cosmic magnetism, dark energy, and dark matter**.
 
• It will use advanced radio astronomy techniques to gather data from **radio waves emitted by celestial objects**.
 
• The SKA will not focus on detecting visible light but will operate in the radio frequency range to uncover insights about the universe.
 
• The project is a collaboration of multiple countries, and it will have facilities in **South Africa and Australia**, not India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cosmic Magnetism:** It refers to the magnetic fields present in space, which influence the formation and evolution of galaxies and other celestial phenomena.
 
• **Dark Matter:** An invisible form of matter that does not emit, absorb, or reflect light, but its presence is inferred from its gravitational effects on visible matter in the universe.
 
• **Radio Astronomy:** A branch of astronomy that studies celestial phenomena by detecting and analyzing radio waves emitted by cosmic objects, such as stars and galaxies.
 
• **SKA Structure:** The Square Kilometer Array will consist of **thousands of antennas** spread across multiple locations to create a combined collecting area of approximately one square kilometer.
 
• **Global Collaboration:** The SKA is supported by an international consortium of countries, including Australia, South Africa, the UK, China, and others, to advance our understanding of the universe.

questions.question: Which curve is typically U-shaped due to the law of variable proportions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Average Variable Cost Curve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Average Variable Cost (AVC) curve is **U-shaped**, as it initially decreases due to increasing returns to the variable factor and later increases due to diminishing returns.
 
• This phenomenon is explained by the **Law of Variable Proportions**, which states that as more units of a variable input are added to a fixed input, the marginal product initially rises and then falls.
 
• The AVC curve reaches its minimum point when **marginal cost equals average variable cost**.
 
• The downward slope of the AVC curve in the initial phase indicates **economies of scale**, while the upward slope reflects diseconomies of scale.
 
• AVC is calculated as total variable cost divided by output: **AVC = TVC/Output**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Variable Proportions:**

 
 
• This economic principle explains how output changes when one input is varied while others are kept constant.
 
• The law operates in three stages: Increasing Returns, Diminishing Returns, and Negative Returns.
 
 
 
• **Marginal Cost (MC):**
 
 
• Marginal Cost refers to the change in total cost resulting from the production of one additional unit of output.
 
• The MC curve intersects the AVC curve at its minimum point.
 
 
 
• **Average Fixed Cost (AFC):**
 
 
• The AFC curve is always downward sloping because fixed costs are spread over increasing units of output.
 
• It is calculated as: AFC = Total Fixed Cost/Output.
 
 
 
• **Total Cost (TC):**
 
 
• Total Cost is the sum of Total Fixed Cost (TFC) and Total Variable Cost (TVC): TC = TFC + TVC.
 
• The shape of the TC curve is influenced by the behavior of TVC, as TFC remains constant.
 
 
 
• **Economies and Diseconomies of Scale:**
 
 
• Economies of scale occur when increased production leads to lower per-unit costs, while diseconomies occur when per-unit costs rise with increased production.
 
• The AVC curve reflects these phases through its U-shape.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor did Maharana Pratap face in the Battle of Haldighati?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Battle of Haldighati was fought on **18 June 1576** between Maharana Pratap of Mewar and the Mughal forces led by **Man Singh I of Amber**, under the command of Emperor Akbar.
 
• It was a short but fierce battle lasting only four hours, symbolizing the resistance of the Rajputs against Mughal dominance.
 
• Maharana Pratap's loyal horse, **Chetak**, played a crucial role in saving him during the battle, becoming a legend in Rajasthani folklore.
 
• Although the Mughals claimed a tactical victory, Maharana Pratap continued his resistance and refused to submit to Akbar throughout his lifetime.
 
• The battle is significant in Indian history as a symbol of courage, valor, and the indomitable spirit of independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Akbar's Expansion Policy:**
 
 
• Akbar aimed to expand the Mughal Empire through diplomacy, alliances, and military conquests.
 
• He sought to integrate Rajput rulers into the Mughal administrative framework, often offering them high-ranking positions in his court.
 
 
 
• **Battlefield of Haldighati:**
 
 
• Haldighati is a narrow mountain pass in the Aravalli Range, located in present-day Rajasthan.
 
• The pass derives its name from the yellow-colored soil resembling turmeric (Haldi* in Hindi).
 
 
 
• **Man Singh I:**

questions.question:
Which of the following is true about the Gudi Padwa festival?

2. The term Gudi refers to a sacred scripture recited on this day.

3. Traditionally, celebrations begin with the consumption of sweets for good luck.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Gudi Padwa** marks the beginning of the Hindu New Year, as per the lunisolar calendar followed in Maharashtra and some other regions of India.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the first day of the Chaitra month, which typically falls in March or April.
 
• The term **"Gudi"** refers to a flag or banner-like structure decorated with a colorful cloth, flowers, and a copper or silver pot, symbolizing victory and prosperity.
 
• It does not involve the recitation of a sacred scripture as implied in the question, nor does the celebration traditionally begin with the consumption of sweets for good luck.
 
• Gudi Padwa is also associated with the arrival of spring and the harvest season, making it a time of joy and renewal for the community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lunisolar Calendar:** The Hindu calendar combines both lunar and solar movements to determine months and years. Gudi Padwa is based on this system.
 
• **Chaitra Navratri:** Gudi Padwa also marks the beginning of Chaitra Navratri, a nine-day festival dedicated to Goddess Durga.
 
• **Symbolism of the Gudi:** The Gudi symbolizes victory and is believed to ward off evil, attract prosperity, and signify the triumph of good over evil.
 
• **Regional Variations:** While Gudi Padwa is celebrated in Maharashtra, similar festivals are observed in other parts of India, such as Ugadi in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, and Cheti Chand among the Sindhi community.
 
• **Cultural Practices:** The festival includes cleaning homes, decorating with rangoli, hoisting the Gudi, and preparing traditional dishes like puran poli and shrikhand.

questions.question: Identify the correct pairing between a plant hormone and its primary physiological function:

options.text: Gibberellin - Stimulating cell division in roots

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethylene - Ripening of fruits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ethylene** is a plant hormone that plays a key role in the **ripening of climacteric fruits**, such as bananas, tomatoes, and apples.
 
• It is the only gaseous plant hormone and is naturally produced by fruits during the ripening process.
 
• Ethylene promotes changes in color, texture, and flavor of fruits by influencing the breakdown of chlorophyll and the conversion of starches to sugars.
 
• It also regulates other processes like **flower senescence** and the shedding of leaves (abscission).
 
• Commercially, ethylene is used to **artificially induce ripening** in fruits post-harvest to meet market demands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gibberellin:**

 
 
• Stimulates stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering.
 
• It plays a key role in breaking seed dormancy and promoting the growth of internodes in plants like sugarcane.
 
 
 
• **Cytokinin:**
 
 
• Primarily regulates **cell division** and promotes shoot growth.
 
• It also delays leaf senescence and works in conjunction with auxins for plant development.
 
 
 
• **Auxin:**
 
 
• Promotes cell elongation, root initiation, and apical dominance.
 
• Auxins are also involved in phototropism and gravitropism, helping plants respond to environmental stimuli.
 
 
 
• **Abscisic Acid (ABA):**
 
 
• Known as the "stress hormone," it regulates stomatal closure during water stress.
 
• ABA induces seed dormancy and is involved in leaf abscission.

• Statement 2 is correct because the Trinity is credited with elevating the kriti form of Carnatic music to its highest artistic and devotional expression.
 
• The kriti form is a structured composition that combines intricate melodies (ragas) with profound lyrics, often devotional in nature.
 
• The Trinity's compositions remain central to Carnatic music performances and pedagogy even today.

• Shobhana Ranade’s legacy of community-driven initiatives mirrors the participatory approach of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, where citizens are actively engaged in improving their surroundings.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct in the context of constitutional interpretation and judicial doctrine?

options.text: The Constitution of India clearly defines the term "basic structure" under Article 368.
The Judiciary rejected the idea of spirit-based interpretation and strictly follows the written text.
The "basic structure" doctrine was brought into existence by the Supreme Court to protect the fundamental features of the Constitution
The Parliament can propose amendments that repeal judicial principles without limitation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The "basic structure" doctrine was brought into existence by the Supreme Court to protect the fundamental features of the Constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "basic structure" doctrine is a judicial principle established by the Supreme Court of India in the landmark **Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala (1973)** case.
 
• This doctrine asserts that while the Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution under Article 368, it cannot alter or destroy its **basic structure**.
 
• The basic structure includes fundamental aspects such as the supremacy of the Constitution, secularism, democracy, rule of law, and the independence of the judiciary.
 
• The doctrine serves as a safeguard to ensure that constitutional amendments do not dilute the essence of the Constitution or violate its core principles.
 
• It empowers the judiciary to review constitutional amendments and strike them down if they infringe upon the basic structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973):** This landmark case established the basic structure doctrine, limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.
 
• **Article 368:** This article of the Indian Constitution provides the procedure for amending the Constitution. However, amendments are subject to the basic structure doctrine.
 
• **Judicial Review:** The power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative acts, including amendments, is integral to maintaining the basic structure.
 
• **Independence of Judiciary:** A fundamental feature of the Constitution, ensuring checks and balances between the legislative, executive, and judiciary branches.
 
• **Spirit-based Interpretation:** The judiciary often interprets the Constitution by considering its overarching principles and values rather than solely relying on the literal text.

• By emphasizing connectivity, IMEC seeks to reduce reliance on China's BRI and provide nations with a more diversified and competitive economic framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI):**

 
 
• An infrastructure development and investment initiative launched by China in 2013.
 
• Aims to create a network of trade routes connecting Asia, Europe, and Africa, often referred to as the "New Silk Road."
 
• BRI includes projects like railways, highways, ports, and energy pipelines, funded by Chinese loans.
 
• Critics often cite concerns about debt traps and lack of transparency in BRI projects.
 
 
 
• **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC):**
 
 
• IMEC was unveiled during the G20 Summit in September 2023, involving India, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the EU, and other partners.
 
• Aims to connect India to Europe via the Middle East through rail and shipping networks.
 
• Focuses on sustainable development, clean energy, and digital connectivity.
 
• Seeks to offer an alternative to China's BRI for global infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of IMEC:**
 
 
• Enhances geopolitical influence of participating nations by creating a new trade route.
 
• Strengthens economic ties between India, the Middle East, and Europe.
 
• Promotes transparent and inclusive economic practices compared to BRI.
 
 
 
• **Global Connectivity Initiatives:**
 
 
• Other notable initiatives include the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP), Asia-Africa Growth Corridor (AAGC), and the Global Gateway by the EU.
 
• These efforts aim to foster sustainable trade and development while reducing dependency on specific countries or regions.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is / are true regarding India's rural and urban population trends from 1901 to 2011

(1) The rural population has consistently increased in absolute numbers.

(2) The percentage share of rural population in total population has steadily declined.

(3) Urban population first exceeded 100 million in 1981.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of the above**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rural population trends (1901-2011):** The rural population of India has consistently increased in absolute numbers over the decades, despite the urbanization trend.
 
• **Decline in rural population share:** While the absolute number of rural residents has grown, their percentage share in the total population has steadily declined due to rapid urbanization and industrialization.
 
• **Urban population milestone:** India's urban population first exceeded 100 million in the census year 1981, marking a significant demographic shift towards urbanization.
 
• **Historical context:** The trends reflect India's socio-economic transformation, including advancements in infrastructure, migration, and economic opportunities in urban centers.
 
• **Data source:** The observations are based on census data collected every decade from 1901 to 2011.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urbanization in India:** Urbanization refers to the increasing population residing in urban areas, primarily driven by migration, industrialization, and better employment opportunities.
 
• **Census of India:** Conducted every 10 years, the census provides valuable demographic data on population trends, literacy, employment, and urban-rural distribution.
 
• **Rural-to-urban migration:** A significant factor in the declining rural population percentage is migration to urban areas for better living standards and job opportunities.
 
• **India's urban population in 2011:** As per the 2011 Census, 31.16% of India’s population lived in urban areas, marking a substantial growth compared to previous decades.
 
• **Future projections:** By 2030, it is projected that nearly 40% of India’s population will reside in urban areas, highlighting the ongoing trend of urbanization.

questions.question: When focusing on a tree while on an anti-clockwise merry-go-round, from which side does it appear and exit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Left**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When you are on an anti-clockwise merry-go-round, your position is constantly changing relative to a stationary object such as a tree.
 
• As the merry-go-round rotates anti-clockwise, the tree will first appear on your right side as you move toward it.
 
• Due to the continuous rotation, the tree will seem to move from your right side to your left side as you pass it.
 
• This apparent motion is a result of the relative positioning between the observer (you) and the stationary object (tree) during the anti-clockwise movement.
 
• The correct interpretation of this phenomenon aligns with the principles of relative motion in physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Relative Motion:** The concept of relative motion describes how the position of an object changes with respect to an observer. In this case, the tree’s apparent motion is relative to the observer’s position on the rotating merry-go-round.
 
• **Anti-clockwise Rotation:** A rotation is termed anti-clockwise when it proceeds in the opposite direction to the movement of clock hands. This impacts the observer’s perception of stationary objects.
 
• **Frame of Reference:** The observer on the merry-go-round is in a non-inertial frame of reference. Stationary objects like the tree appear to move due to the observer’s rotational motion.
 
• **Perception of Motion:** The apparent movement of the tree from right to left is a result of the observer’s changing position and orientation relative to the tree.
 
• **Practical Example:** Similar observations can be made in other rotational systems, such as carousels or spinning platforms, where objects appear to move in a direction opposite to the rotation.

questions.question: What does the term "Duckworth-Lewis Method relate to in cricket ?

options.text: Calculating revised target in rain-affected matches

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calculating revised target in rain-affected matches**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Duckworth-Lewis Method is a mathematical formula used in cricket to calculate a revised target score in rain-affected matches where overs are lost.
 
• It was introduced by statisticians Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis in 1997 and is now officially known as the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method after updates by Professor Steven Stern.
 
• The method takes into account the number of overs remaining and the number of wickets lost to produce a fair target for the chasing team.
 
• It has been adopted by the International Cricket Council (ICC) for use in limited-overs matches, including One-Day Internationals (ODIs) and Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is).
 
• The DLS method ensures fairness by considering both resources (overs and wickets) available to the batting team at any point during the match.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis:** The original developers of the method aimed to address the shortcomings of previous rain-rule systems in cricket, such as the "most productive overs" method.
 
• **Steven Stern's Contribution:** Professor Steven Stern updated the Duckworth-Lewis method in 2015 to reflect modern cricket scoring patterns, leading to its renaming as the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method.
 
• **Key Principles:** The method uses pre-determined tables based on historical data to estimate the resources (overs and wickets) a team has left in a match, providing a fair revised target.
 
• **Criticism:** While widely used, the DLS method has faced criticism for its complexity and occasional perceived unfairness in scenarios of extreme weather interruptions.
 
• **Alternatives:** Other rain rules, such as the "VJD Method" (used in domestic cricket in India), also exist but have not gained the same level of global acceptance as the DLS method.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act made the Right to Education a Fundamental Right in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Amendment Act, 2002**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **86th Amendment Act, 2002** inserted Article 21A into the Constitution, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right.
 
• It mandates free and compulsory education for children aged **6 to 14 years** in India.
 
• This amendment led to the enactment of the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009**.
 
• Article 21A ensures that education is provided as a fundamental right, emphasizing equal access for all children irrespective of background.
 
• The amendment also modified Article 45 to prioritize early childhood care and education for children below six years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21A:** It obligates the State to provide free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years.
 
• **RTE Act, 2009:** Enacted to operationalize Article 21A, it specifies norms, standards, and rights related to education.
 
• **Changes to Article 45:** It shifted focus from universal primary education to early childhood care and education.
 
• **Fundamental Rights:** The Right to Education under Article 21A is categorized as a Fundamental Right, ensuring legal enforceability.
 
• **India's Education Policy:** The amendment marked a significant milestone in India’s efforts to achieve universal education and literacy.
